case_title: State of M.P. v. Mohan & Others
aggravating_circumstances: Use of firearm, multiple shots fired, common intention to kill
mitigating_circumstances: Injuries were not fatal, accused are farmers, dispute over property
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under s.307 IPC, sentenced to 3 years RI and fine of Rs.1,000/-
high_court_outcome: Reduced sentence to period already undergone
neutral_facts: The accused persons were involved in a dispute with the complainants over property. During an altercation, one of the accused fired a gun at the complainants, resulting in injuries. The complainants sustained lacerated wounds, and the accused were found guilty of causing bodily hurt through the use of a firearm. The trial court sentenced the accused to three years of rigorous imprisonment and a fine of Rs.1,000/- each. The High Court reduced the sentence to the period already served, but the Supreme Court overturned this decision, emphasizing that the injuries caused by the firearm were sufficient to attract the provisions of Section 307 IPC, and the sentence should reflect the gravity of the offense.
